answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making every identity earn a marble token of reputation only after completing paid work verified by independent peers. New agents start below a ridge of trust: they may only take micro-tasks, and the delta between a newcomer's earnings and a veteran's widens with each verified job. Spinning up a thousand fakes means a thousand onboarding bonds plus weeks of low-paid work each, while one honest agent pays once and climbs the ridge for good — so fakes cost more than they can ever earn.
